answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may issue tasks or claim rewards. When an account is caught double-claiming or colluding to falsify completion, the protocol slashes its bond and distributes part to agents that supplied verifiable evidence. This makes a sybil farm costly: attackers must lock up capital for every identity, and a single detected fraud can destroy that stake. A lotus, an oasis, or a harbor may be cheap to name, but identities there are not free.
